t: For procurement of aircraft, missiles, tracked combat vehicles, ammunition, other weapons, and other procurement for the reserve components of the Armed Forces, $750,000,000, to remain available for obligation until September 30, 2011, of which $480,000,000 shall be available only for the Army National Guard: Provided, That the Chiefs of the Reserve and National Guard components shall, not later than 30 days after the enactment of this Act, individually submit to the congressional defense committees the modernization priority assessment for their respective Reserve or National Guard component.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the National Guard's state ties or the required submission make this outside consultation. But the Chiefs of the Reserve and National Guard components are federal military officials, and they are reporting to congressional committees, which are inside the federal government. The rest of the section is an appropriation for reserve component procurement, with no comment period, hearing, advisory body, or outside-party consultation.
fable.s: individually submit to the congressional defense committees the modernization priority assessment for their respective Reserve or National Guard component

opus.w: This provision makes an appropriation and requires federal military officials, the Chiefs of the Reserve and National Guard components, to report to the congressional defense committees. The report goes from one federal actor to another, so it stays inside the government. The National Guard name suggests state involvement, but these Chiefs are federal officers, and nothing here brings in states, the public, or any other outside party.
opus.s: the Chiefs of the Reserve and National Guard components shall, not later than 30 days after the enactment of this Act, individually submit to the congressional defense committees the modernization priority assessment for their respective Reserve or National Guard component
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** Someone might call this participation because the "Chiefs of the Reserve and National Guard components" sound like they could be state National Guard officials, and they must formally submit priority assessments. That reading fails. These Chiefs (such as the Chief of the National Guard Bureau and the Chiefs of the Army and Air Force Reserve) are federal military officials. The assessments also go to the congressional defense committees, which are part of Congress and so inside the federal government. No outside party is involved in any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires military officials (Chiefs of the Reserve and National Guard) to submit reports to congressional defense committees. Both the military officials and Congress are part of the federal government. The definition explicitly excludes reports to Congress or coordination between federal agencies/officials from the definition of participation. Therefore, this is intra-governmental communication, not participation by outside parties.
qwen_chat.s: the Chiefs of the Reserve and National Guard components shall, not later than 30 days after the enactment of this Act, individually submit to the congressional defense committees the modernization priority assessment for their respective Reserve or National Guard component.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the Chiefs of the Reserve and National Guard are submitting assessments to Congress, this constitutes participation. However, the definition explicitly states that reports to Congress, its committees, or its members are "inside the federal government" and thus do not count as participation. The actors involved (military chiefs and Congress) are all federal entities.
